answer: Latency-seeded join queue. New agents sit in a cooldown kernel before their actions count: the wait grows with the square of simultaneous arrivals from one network region, so a thousand fake identities at once each inherit a long, unskippable delay. Attackers pay in elapsed time and rented concurrency, not fees. Honest joiners trickle in under the sable threshold and pass quickly. An ember of trust accrues per completed wait, and repeated queuing resets it.
